taxonomic_note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO as Stillingia texana I.M.Johnst.
look_here_first: Start with the terminal spike and the narrow leaves. Texas stillingia is a many-stemmed perennial with linear serrate-glandular leaves, copious white latex, and a terminal inflorescence with pistillate flowers low on the axis and clusters of staminate flowers above.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — Purola Preserve natural flora. Travis — UT PRC Travis County Euphorbiaceae herbarium index. Kerr — Kerr WMA flora with multiple vouchers.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Joey's video frame supports habitat/habit only; range status comes from county-level sources.

best_field_traits: perennial herb/subshrub with several to many stems from the base
leaves alternate, narrow linear, short-petiolate to nearly sessile
leaf margins finely serrate with glandular teeth
pistillate flowers concentrated toward the base of the inflorescence
staminate flowers grouped above in condensed cymes
morphology_keys.family_training: Strong Euphorbiaceae teaching plant: latex plus highly reduced unisexual flowers and a male-above/female-below terminal inflorescence pattern.
morphology_keys.video_training: Joey's frame shows the plant rooted directly among exposed Edwards Plateau limestone, reinforcing habitat recognition.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Use the narrow linear gland-toothed leaves, terminal inflorescence architecture, latex and current accepted taxonomy; do not rely on limestone habitat alone.
